item.title: Verona Park — Sat Sep 5, 9:30 AM
item.description:
Let's Walk!! JOIN US FOR A WALK
We will meet at the benches in front of the boathouse.
We will walk the loop around the park. The goal will be at least three miles, but there is plenty of opportunity to stop or continue to fit your personal goals.
We will be walking on a paved surface.
We walk at a medium speed.
Please plan to arrive 5 minutes **early** so that we can **start on time.**
Verona Park is 54.32 acres with a lake running through it. It is bordered by Lakeside and Bloomfield Avenues in the southern part of Verona. It is the fifth largest park in the Essex County system, making it a great place to walk.
Disclaimer: If you join us for a hike, please understand that you are responsible for your own preparedness and well-being and will hold no one else liable in case of injury or mishap. Event will be canceled in the event of extreme weather.
Source: Meetup: Let's Walk!!

item.title: Inner Body Meditation (20 minutes) — Thu Sep 10, 9:30 PM
item.description:
The Mindful Stream "Awareness of the inner body takes you beyond the mind." - Eckhart Tolle
In this mediation session we will bring our attention here: to the inner body. Sessions are suitable for newcomers, those experienced in Tolle's teachings and anyone wishing to remain completely anonymous. They will last around 20 minutes and cameras and microphones will be disabled. (Depending on the situation, a free discussion may be held at the end with mics and cameras allowed.)
See you there!
Please be aware that sessions will close if no members have joined after 10 minutes.
Emrys also organises a free Work of Byron Katie online mediation group. Visit [this Meetup Group link](https://www.meetup.com/thework-runsfree/) for more information.21
Source: Meetup: The Mindful Stream

item.title: Kichwa Language Workshop Series — Mon Sep 14, 5:30 PM — Cole Hall # 141
item.description:
LAIC (LATIN AMERICAN INDIGENOUS COLLABORATIVE) at CLaSE invites the Montclair State University community and the broader public to participate in our Kichwa Language & Culture Workshop Series, beginning Monday, September 14. This 10-week workshop series offers participants the opportunity to learn Kichwa while exploring the language, culture, and traditions of Kichwa-speaking communities. Workshops are conducted in Spanish and Kichwa by our amazing and well known Kichwa community leaders - Atik Paguay and Fabian Muenala and are open to students, faculty, staff, families, and community members from outside the University. No previous knowledge of Kichwa is required. Mondays, beginning September 145:30–7:30 p.m.Cole Hall, Room 14110-week series We invite everyone interested in Indigenous languages and cultures to join us. Registration is required by contacting Dr. Calarota-Ninman at calarotaa@montclair.edu
Hosted by: Center for Latino Heritage & Spanish Language Excellence

item.title: Accounting Society - Al-Nesha Jones, CPA, MBA — Wed Sep 16, 2:00 PM — SBUS 255 Feliciano School of Business
item.description:
Our Story - ASE Group
Our founder, Al-Nesha Jones, CPA, MBA, MOM, started ASE Group as the solution she needed to create freedom and flexibility as a working mom. With over a decade of experience in corporate America, she understood the importance of streamlining systems, financial reporting, and analytics, and she knew it could be done without having to sacrifice being present with her family. She was on a personal pursuit for flexibility and financial freedom, and a professional quest to serve her community in an impactful way.
SBUS 255 (School of Business). We look forward to seeing you on September 16th.

item.title: Wildflower Sculpture Park Opening Reception — Sun Sep 20, 3:00 PM
item.description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group The [Wildflower Sculpture Park](https://www.somocon.org/visit/wildflower-sculpture-park/?mc_cid=887616f7ab&mc_eid=UNIQID) invites you to the opening of this year’s project, **Root System**, a collaborative, site-responsive exploration of roots, rhizomes, and interconnected systems of life.
Curatorial and artist talk will begin at 3:30pm. Light refreshments will be served.
Artists were encouraged to consider how ecological networks within the South Mountain Reservation connect to community, history, and ancestry, and to propose work that engages themes of resilience, symbiosis, and environmental stewardship.
Presenting artists: ANONDA BELL CORRINE CARR CHRISTINE DACRUZ KATE EGGLESTON SAMAR HUSSAINI HAMEWS KAREN LEO ALESSANDRA PUGLISI JIMENA VEGA WILLA VUCETAJ
Questions? [wildflowersculpture@somocon.org](mailto:wildflowersculpture@somocon.org)
Source: Meetup: South Mountain Conservancy

item.description:
The Dominoes Tournament is a Hispanic Heritage Month event hosted by Lambda Theta Phi where students will compete in teams in a dominoes tournament. Teams will first compete in smaller groups before the top teams advance to the semifinals and championship round. The event will also include music, food, and opportunities for students to socialize while celebrating the cultural importance of dominoes within the Latino community. The goal is to create a fun and welcoming event that brings students together through culture and friendly competition.

item.title: Tech Toolbox — Tue Nov 3, 12:30 PM — Montclair Main - Classroom
item.description:
Tech Toolbox is a free hands-on workshop series focused on building real, practical digital skills. Each session zeroes in on a specific skill, program, or tool—from core computer skills and file management to navigating software and online platforms you use every day. Participants are encouraged to bring their own devices and follow along, so you'll leave each session having actually practiced what you learned.
All experience levels are welcome, and your instructor will be there to walk you through everything step by step. Sessions are free and open to the public.
This week's topic is: TBD
Source: Libcal Bccls 10306

item.title: Tech Talks — Tue Nov 3, 3:30 PM — Montclair Main - Classroom
item.description:
Tech Talks is a free informational series where library staff introduce and explain the technology topics that matter most in today's digital world. Each session takes a closer look at a new or complex topic—whether it's a trending app, an emerging technology, or a platform you've been hearing about but aren't quite sure how to navigate. Through demonstrations and clear, jargon-free explanations, you'll come away with a better understanding of the tech landscape around you. There's no hands-on component, so no devices are needed—just come ready to learn and ask questions.
All are welcome regardless of experience level, and time is reserved at the end of each session for Q&A. Sessions are free and open to the public.
This week's topic is: TBD
Source: Libcal Bccls 10306

item.description:

Join us in the Sundays of Advent as we wait in expectancy for the Christ-child once again.
